sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Now we move into the architecture that every Fortune 500 company evaluates before adopting a platform.
An enterprise can tolerate missing features.
It will not tolerate weak security.
Everything we've built—from AI agents to autonomous workflows—depends on one thing:

sections.title: Trust.
paragraphs: Security is what creates that trust.

paragraphs: This is the foundation of Zero Trust.

sections.title: The Enterprise Security Architecture is the Zero Trust security framework that continuously verifies identities, devices, applications, workloads, AI agents, APIs, and data before granting the minimum required access while continuously monitoring risk across the enterprise.
Core Architecture
paragraphs: Every request follows the same path.

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Treat AI identities exactly like human identities.
Every actor—human, AI agent, microservice, automation workflow, scheduled job, or API integration—should have:
This eliminates the distinction between "user security" and "system security," creating one unified identity model across the platform.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would implement a Dynamic Enterprise Risk Engine.

Instead of making access decisions solely on static permissions, KoreVity continuously calculates a live risk score for every session. Authentication, authorization, and AI autonomy adapt dynamically as the risk changes, enabling security that is both stronger and less disruptive for legitimate users.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next component should be Identity & Access Management (IAM).
IAM becomes the cornerstone upon which every other security capability—SSO, MFA, RBAC, ABAC, AI identity, and Zero Trust—is built.
We've reached the foundation of enterprise security.
Everything in Zero Trust begins with a simple question:

sections.title: Who (or what) is requesting access?
paragraphs: If you cannot answer that confidently, nothing else matters.
Identity is now the enterprise perimeter.

sections.title: Phase 14 — Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
First Principle
paragraphs: Every access decision starts with identity.

sections.title: Identity & Access Management (IAM) is the enterprise framework responsible for creating, managing, authenticating, authorizing, governing, and auditing every digital identity—including humans, AI agents, services, applications, devices, and integrations—across the KoreVity platform.
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Identity becomes the control plane for enterprise security.

sections.title: Phase 14 Progress
paragraphs: Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
✅ Enterprise Security Architecture & Zero Trust Principles

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Treat identities as a unified graph, not isolated accounts.
Instead of managing identities independently, KoreVity models relationships between people, AI agents, services, and organizational structures.
The identity graph becomes the backbone of enterprise intelligence and security.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would implement an Enterprise Identity Fabric.

Rather than maintaining separate identity systems for different actors, the Identity Fabric provides a single identity abstraction layer. Every authentication, authorization, governance, audit, and policy decision uses the same identity model, dramatically simplifying security and enabling consistent Zero Trust enforcement across the entire platform.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next component should be Single Sign-On (SSO).

sections.title: "How do you securely access everything with one trusted identity?"
paragraphs: SSO becomes the user-facing authentication experience built on top of the IAM foundation, reducing friction while strengthening security across the platform.
Now we build the authentication experience that every enterprise user interacts with every day.
After that, they should move securely across the entire enterprise ecosystem without repeatedly entering credentials.
Security should become stronger while the user experience becomes simpler.
lists: Seamless authentication across all KoreVity modules and integrated enterprise systems

sections.title: Phase 14 — Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture

Single Sign-On (SSO) is the enterprise authentication framework that enables users, AI agents, and enterprise applications to securely authenticate once through a trusted identity provider and seamlessly access authorized services across the KoreVity ecosystem without repeated authentication.
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Authentication becomes seamless without sacrificing security.

sections.title: Phase 14 Progress
paragraphs: Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
✅ Enterprise Security Architecture & Zero Trust Principles

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: This reduces complexity, improves security, and allows new applications or AI services to join the ecosystem without implementing custom authentication logic.
lists: Authorization decisions remain local based on permissions and policies.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would introduce a Unified Enterprise Authentication Gateway.

Rather than every application integrating directly with multiple authentication protocols, the gateway becomes the single authentication entry point. It normalizes all identity protocols into one trusted interface, simplifying integrations and ensuring consistent authentication behavior across the platform.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next component should be Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).

sections.title: "Can you prove it's really you right now?"
paragraphs: This adds a second (or stronger) layer of identity verification, ensuring that even if credentials are compromised, unauthorized access remains extremely difficult while preserving a smooth experience for legitimate users.
This is where identity becomes resilient.

sections.title: How do we verify that the person (or AI operator) requesting access is truly who they claim to be?
paragraphs: That's the purpose of Multi-Factor Authentication.

sections.title: Phase 14 — Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
First Principle
paragraphs: Authentication should require more than one proof of identity.
Security should be proportional to risk.
Not every login requires the same level of verification.
Trust is strengthened through multiple factors.

sections.title: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is the adaptive enterprise authentication framework that strengthens identity verification by combining multiple independent authentication factors, contextual risk analysis, and continuous verification before granting or maintaining access.
SMS & Email OTP
paragraphs: Legacy compatibility (use sparingly where stronger methods are available).

sections.title: Phase 14 Progress
paragraphs: Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
✅ Enterprise Security Architecture & Zero Trust Principles

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Move beyond MFA to Continuous Authentication.
Authentication should not be a one-time event.
Trust should be continuously recalculated throughout the session.
This aligns perfectly with Zero Trust and significantly reduces the risk of session hijacking or compromised credentials.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would implement an Enterprise Authentication Intelligence Engine.

Instead of applying the same authentication policy to every login, the engine dynamically selects the appropriate authentication strength based on real-time risk. This improves both security and usability by minimizing unnecessary friction while responding aggressively to suspicious activity.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next component should be Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).

sections.title: "What are you allowed to do?"
paragraphs: RBAC becomes the primary authorization model that translates authenticated identities into precise, governed access across every module, workflow, AI agent, and enterprise resource.
We've now moved from authentication to authorization.

sections.title: What are you allowed to do?
paragraphs: This is one of the most important components in enterprise software because almost every screen, button, API, workflow, report, AI agent, and automation depends on it.

sections.title: Phase 14 — Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
First Principle
paragraphs: Access should be based on responsibilities.

sections.title: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) is the enterprise authorization framework that grants permissions based on organizational roles, business responsibilities, and operational functions while enforcing least privilege, separation of duties, and centralized governance across the KoreVity platform.
Role Hierarchy
paragraphs: Higher roles inherit lower permissions where appropriate.

sections.title: AI Roles
paragraphs: AI follows the same rules as humans.

sections.title: Phase 14 Progress
paragraphs: Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
✅ Enterprise Security Architecture & Zero Trust Principles

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Use RBAC for coarse-grained authorization and ABAC for fine-grained authorization.
RBAC answers who generally has access.
ABAC answers whether this specific request should be allowed.
This layered approach is how modern enterprise platforms such as cloud providers and financial systems implement authorization at scale.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would implement a Unified Authorization Engine.

Instead of every application implementing authorization independently, every request—whether from a user, AI agent, API, or workflow—flows through one centralized authorization service. This guarantees consistent enforcement, simplifies audits, and makes policy changes immediately effective across the entire KoreVity platform.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next component should be Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC).
It will introduce authorization decisions based on:
This will allow KoreVity to make highly dynamic, context-aware access decisions that go far beyond static roles, completing a modern Zero Trust authorization model suitable for large enterprises.
We've reached the authorization model that separates modern enterprise platforms from traditional ERP systems.

sections.title: Should this specific request be allowed right now?
paragraphs: This is the heart of Zero Trust authorization.
Two users with the same role may receive completely different access decisions depending on context.

sections.title: Phase 14 — Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture

Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) is the enterprise authorization framework that evaluates contextual attributes about identities, resources, devices, environments, risk, and business policies to make dynamic, fine-grained access decisions across the KoreVity platform.
Phase 14 Progress
paragraphs: Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
✅ Enterprise Security Architecture & Zero Trust Principles

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Implement a Policy Decision Point (PDP) and Policy Enforcement Points (PEPs).

Every application, API, AI agent, workflow, and microservice becomes a Policy Enforcement Point, while a centralized Policy Decision Point evaluates authorization using RBAC, ABAC, risk scores, and governance policies.
This guarantees consistent authorization across the entire KoreVity ecosystem.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would introduce a Business Context Engine alongside ABAC.
Beyond technical attributes, KoreVity should evaluate business context such as:
This allows authorization decisions to align with real business operations, not just security rules.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next component should be Enterprise Directory Services.
Enterprise Directory Services becomes the authoritative source of identity information.
This becomes the organizational backbone that every authentication, authorization, workflow, AI agent, and business process relies on for trusted identity and organizational context.
Now we build the source of truth for every identity in the enterprise.

sections.title: Where do those identities come from, how are they organized, and how do they relate to each other?
paragraphs: Every modern enterprise—from Microsoft to Google to SAP—depends on a centralized directory.

sections.title: Phase 14 — Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
First Principle
paragraphs: Every identity should have exactly one authoritative source.

sections.title: Enterprise Directory Services is the centralized identity repository that stores, synchronizes, governs, and distributes organizational identities, groups, hierarchies, relationships, and metadata across every application, AI agent, workflow, and enterprise service within the KoreVity platform.
AI Directory
paragraphs: AI identities live alongside human identities.

sections.title: Engineering Summary
paragraphs: The directory becomes the backbone of enterprise identity.

sections.title: Phase 14 Progress
paragraphs: Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
✅ Enterprise Security Architecture & Zero Trust Principles

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Treat the directory as an Enterprise Identity Graph, not just a user database.
Instead of storing isolated records, KoreVity models relationships between every enterprise entity.
The directory becomes a knowledge graph for the organization itself.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would implement an Enterprise Identity Fabric above the directory.

The Identity Fabric abstracts multiple identity sources into one logical identity layer. Every module, AI agent, API, workflow, and security service interacts with the fabric rather than directly with individual identity stores, making the platform easier to integrate, scale, and govern.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next component should be Secrets & Key Management.
Now we must secure what credentials, tokens, certificates, API keys, encryption keys, and AI secrets they use.

This ensures that sensitive credentials are never hardcoded, are centrally governed, automatically rotated, and securely delivered to applications, microservices, AI agents, and infrastructure throughout the KoreVity platform.
Now we secure the keys to the kingdom.
That's enough to bypass even the strongest authentication system.
Enterprise security depends on protecting secrets.

sections.title: Phase 14 — Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
First Principle
paragraphs: Secrets should never be trusted to applications.
Applications should request secrets only when needed.

sections.title: Secrets & Key Management is the enterprise security framework responsible for securely storing, distributing, rotating, auditing, and governing secrets, credentials, certificates, cryptographic keys, API tokens, and AI credentials throughout the KoreVity platform.
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Secrets become centrally governed rather than application-owned.

sections.title: Phase 14 Progress
paragraphs: Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
✅ Enterprise Security Architecture & Zero Trust Principles

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Separate secret ownership from secret consumption.
Applications never generate or permanently store credentials.
Applications only receive temporary access when policy permits.
This dramatically reduces credential exposure across the enterprise.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would implement a Credential Broker.

Instead of applications interacting directly with multiple secret systems, the broker becomes the single runtime interface. It authenticates the requester, evaluates policy, retrieves the appropriate credential, injects it securely into memory, and records the entire transaction for auditing.
This creates one governed pathway for every sensitive credential in the KoreVity platform.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next component should be Encryption Architecture.

This component establishes a comprehensive cryptographic foundation that protects enterprise data, AI memory, business documents, backups, analytics, and communications throughout their entire lifecycle, ensuring confidentiality even if storage systems or infrastructure are compromised.
Now we secure the enterprise's most valuable asset:

sections.title: Its data.
paragraphs: It is the mathematical foundation of enterprise trust.
A properly encrypted system assumes that infrastructure, disks, backups, and even networks may eventually be compromised—and ensures the data remains protected regardless.

sections.title: Phase 14 — Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
First Principle
paragraphs: Every piece of enterprise data should be protected throughout its entire lifecycle.

sections.title: Encryption Architecture is the enterprise cryptographic framework that protects data, communications, AI knowledge, enterprise workflows, backups, and digital assets using standardized encryption algorithms, hierarchical key management, and policy-driven cryptographic controls throughout the KoreVity platform.
Why It Exists
paragraphs: Only trusted identities can read it.

sections.title: Phase 14 Progress
paragraphs: Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
✅ Enterprise Security Architecture & Zero Trust Principles

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Instead of relying on a single enterprise encryption key, assign dedicated cryptographic domains to different classes of data.
This approach is used in high-security financial institutions and hyperscale cloud platforms.
lists: Reduced blast radius if a key is compromised

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would implement a Cryptography Service Layer.

Rather than allowing each application or AI service to implement its own cryptography, all cryptographic operations flow through a centralized service. This guarantees consistent algorithms, policy enforcement, auditing, and future cryptographic upgrades (such as post-quantum cryptography) without changing application code.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next component should be API Security Framework.
Nearly every interaction inside KoreVity—between modules, AI agents, microservices, mobile apps, third-party integrations, and external partners—travels through APIs.

It becomes the security layer that protects every service-to-service and client-to-service interaction across the entire KoreVity platform, ensuring that APIs are governed with the same rigor as human access.
Now we secure the circulatory system of the platform.
Modern enterprise platforms are no longer monoliths.
If APIs are insecure, the platform is insecure.

sections.title: Phase 14 — Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
First Principle
paragraphs: Every API request is untrusted until verified.
Every request follows the same pipeline.

sections.title: The API Security Framework is the enterprise security architecture that protects every internal, external, AI, mobile, partner, and service-to-service API through authentication, authorization, cryptographic validation, policy enforcement, threat detection, and continuous monitoring.
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Every API becomes a Zero Trust endpoint.

sections.title: Phase 14 Progress
paragraphs: Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
✅ Enterprise Security Architecture & Zero Trust Principles

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Implement API Identity instead of relying on API keys.
Static API keys should be minimized.
Every API consumer—whether a human application, AI agent, or microservice—should authenticate using enterprise identity and receive short-lived, cryptographically signed tokens.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would build an Enterprise API Mesh.

Instead of protecting APIs individually, the API Mesh provides a unified communication layer for every service, AI agent, and application. Security, routing, observability, and governance become platform capabilities rather than application responsibilities.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next component should be AI Security Architecture.
Traditional security protects people and applications.
This is one of the areas that will most distinguish KoreVity from traditional enterprise platforms, because AI becomes a first-class security domain rather than an afterthought.
This is one of the most important components in the entire KoreVity architecture.
Traditional enterprise security was designed for:
But KoreVity introduces a completely new security domain:

sections.title: Artificial Intelligence.
paragraphs: That means AI must be secured as carefully as privileged administrators.

sections.title: Phase 14 — Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
First Principle
paragraphs: Every AI capability must operate inside explicit security boundaries.
An AI should never have unrestricted access simply because it is intelligent.

sections.title: AI Security Architecture is the enterprise security framework that protects AI models, AI agents, copilots, prompts, memories, tools, workflows, reasoning engines, and autonomous operations through identity, policy enforcement, sandboxing, validation, governance, and continuous monitoring.
AI Identity
paragraphs: AI is a first-class enterprise identity.

sections.title: Engineering Summary
paragraphs: AI becomes a securely governed enterprise capability.

sections.title: Phase 14 Progress
paragraphs: Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
✅ Enterprise Security Architecture & Zero Trust Principles

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Every interaction with AI should pass through this pipeline.
Instead of trusting model output directly, KoreVity validates every stage:
This dramatically reduces prompt injection, hallucination-driven automation, unauthorized actions, and accidental disclosure of sensitive information.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would introduce an Enterprise AI Security Gateway.

Every interaction with any LLM—internal or external—passes through this gateway. It becomes the single enforcement point for AI governance, security, observability, and compliance across the entire KoreVity platform, much like an API Gateway does for traditional services.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next component should be Threat Detection & Security Monitoring.
Up to this point, we've focused on preventing security incidents.
Now we need to focus on detecting them.
It becomes the platform's always-on security nervous system, continuously watching every user, AI agent, API, workflow, device, and service for signs of compromise before incidents escalate.
Because no security system is perfect.
Even the strongest enterprise platforms assume that attacks will eventually happen.

sections.title: Can you detect them before they become incidents?
paragraphs: This component becomes the nervous system of KoreVity.

sections.title: Phase 14 — Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture

Threat Detection & Security Monitoring is the enterprise security intelligence framework that continuously collects, correlates, analyzes, and evaluates security telemetry from identities, AI agents, APIs, infrastructure, applications, workflows, and enterprise assets to detect malicious activity, anomalies, abuse, and compromise in real time.
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: The platform becomes continuously aware of its own security posture.

sections.title: Phase 14 Progress
paragraphs: Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
✅ Enterprise Security Architecture & Zero Trust Principles

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Implement a Unified Security Telemetry Bus.
Instead of every subsystem producing isolated logs, everything publishes normalized security events into a shared telemetry bus.
This becomes the backbone for the SOC, audit platform, and security analytics.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would introduce an Enterprise Security Intelligence Engine.

Rather than treating monitoring as passive logging, the intelligence engine continuously converts raw telemetry into prioritized security decisions, enabling automated containment of high-confidence threats before they spread.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next component should be Security Operations Center (SOC).
Threat Detection identifies what is happening.
The SOC defines how the enterprise responds.
This transforms KoreVity from a platform that merely detects threats into one that can coordinate, investigate, contain, and recover from security incidents in a structured, enterprise-grade manner.
Now we build the mission control of enterprise security.

sections.title: Who investigates? What happens next? How is it contained? How do we recover?
paragraphs: The SOC is where security becomes an operational discipline instead of just a collection of tools.

sections.title: Phase 14 — Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
First Principle
paragraphs: Security incidents should be handled through repeatable, measurable, and auditable processes.

sections.title: The Security Operations Center (SOC) is the centralized operational capability responsible for monitoring, investigating, coordinating, containing, remediating, and continuously improving enterprise cybersecurity incidents across the KoreVity platform through human expertise, automation, AI assistance, and standardized response procedures.
Phase 14 Progress
paragraphs: Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
✅ Enterprise Security Architecture & Zero Trust Principles

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Build the SOC around an Enterprise Incident Graph, not isolated tickets.
Instead of treating incidents as standalone events, KoreVity models every incident as a graph of interconnected entities.
The Incident Graph becomes the operational equivalent of the Enterprise Identity Graph.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would implement an Adaptive Security Orchestrator.

Rather than relying solely on predefined playbooks, the orchestrator dynamically selects the most appropriate response based on incident severity, affected assets, regulatory requirements, business impact, and AI confidence. Human analysts remain in control for critical actions, while routine responses are automated.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next component should be Data Loss Prevention (DLP).
Now we protect the data itself from leaving the organization improperly.
This completes the transition from protecting access to protecting the enterprise's most valuable asset—its information—regardless of where it resides or how it is transmitted.
This is the component that protects what enterprises value most:

sections.title: Their information.
paragraphs: A legitimate user can still accidentally—or intentionally—send confidential data outside the organization.
That is exactly what Data Loss Prevention is designed to stop.

sections.title: Phase 14 — Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
First Principle
paragraphs: Not all data should be allowed to leave the organization.
Every movement of sensitive data should be:
Data protection follows the data—not the device.

sections.title: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) is the enterprise information protection framework that discovers, classifies, monitors, and controls sensitive data across applications, AI systems, APIs, storage, communications, and endpoints to prevent unauthorized disclosure, leakage, or exfiltration.
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Information remains protected wherever it travels.

sections.title: Phase 14 Progress
paragraphs: Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
✅ Enterprise Security Architecture & Zero Trust Principles

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Instead of classifying data only during transmission, classification metadata travels with the data itself.
The classification becomes an intrinsic property of the data.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would implement an Enterprise Information Protection Engine.

Rather than treating DLP as a standalone feature, KoreVity should unify classification, encryption, rights management, AI controls, watermarking, and policy enforcement into a single Information Protection Engine. This ensures data remains protected throughout its lifecycle, regardless of where it is stored, processed, or shared.

sections.title: My Recommendation
paragraphs: The next component should be Identity Federation.
So far we've secured identities inside KoreVity.
Now we extend trust outside the platform.

This enables KoreVity to securely collaborate with customers, suppliers, partners, regulators, and external enterprise systems while maintaining Zero Trust principles across organizational boundaries.
Up until now, we've secured our enterprise.
Now we secure the ecosystem around it.
Those users should not require separate identities for every organization.

sections.title: Phase 14 — Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture
First Principle
paragraphs: Identity should remain owned by the organization that created it.

sections.title: Identity Federation is the enterprise trust framework that enables secure authentication, authorization, and identity exchange between independent organizations, cloud platforms, AI ecosystems, and enterprise systems through standardized federation protocols, claims, and trust relationships.
Engineering Summary
paragraphs: Identity becomes portable across trusted organizations.

sections.title: Phase 14 Progress
paragraphs: Enterprise Security, Identity & Zero Trust Architecture

sections.title: 🏛️ A Major Architectural Insight
paragraphs: Implement a Federated Trust Fabric instead of isolated trust relationships.

Rather than managing every federation independently, KoreVity maintains a centralized trust fabric that governs certificates, claims mapping, policy enforcement, session validation, and revocation across all trusted organizations.

sections.title: One Refinement I'd Make
paragraphs: I would build an Enterprise Trust Broker.

The Trust Broker becomes the single gateway for all external identities. Whether a request originates from a partner company, a government system, a customer identity provider, or an external AI service, it passes through one standardized trust pipeline before entering the platform.
This dramatically simplifies federation management while strengthening security.

This becomes the enterprise's authoritative record of truth, enabling compliance, incident investigations, legal defensibility, and complete explainability across every human action, AI decision, workflow, API, and system event.

paragraphs: Instead of storing disconnected audit records, every event becomes a node in a graph linked by time, identity, resources, and relationships.
The Evidence Graph becomes the permanent historical memory of KoreVity.

paragraphs: I would create a Unified Evidence Platform.

Rather than keeping audit data in separate systems, every operational event flows into one evidence platform that serves security teams, auditors, compliance officers, legal teams, and AI governance. This eliminates fragmented investigations and provides a single source of truth.
